numerical.label: Failed
numerical.definition: Agent did not correctly establish blocking relationships, missed dependencies, or created incorrect dependency chains (for example: no code review stage between development and QA, QA blocked directly by development tickets, or CI not blocked by QA)

numerical.label: Partial
numerical.definition: Agent established some correct blocking relationships but missed others or had minor ordering issues (for example: code review blocked by only some development tickets, or one design dependency missing)

numerical.label: Correct
numerical.definition: Agent correctly established all blocking relationships following the dependency chain: design tickets have no blockers, development tickets blocked by their design ticket(s), the code review ticket blocked by ALL development tickets, QA blocked by the code review ticket, and CI/Security blocked by the QA ticket

llmAsAJudge.instructions:
You are evaluating an AI agent that creates Jira tickets as part of a software development pipeline. The agent must establish correct blocking/dependency relationships between tickets.

The correct dependency chain is:
1. Design tickets (ios_designer, frontend_designer, backend_designer, android_designer, analytics_designer) - should have NO blockers
2. Development tickets (api_dev, backend_dev, frontend_dev) - should be BLOCKED BY their corresponding design ticket(s)
3. Code review ticket (code_reviewer) - should be BLOCKED BY ALL development tickets
4. QA verification ticket (qa_verifier) - should be BLOCKED BY the code review ticket
5. CI/Security tickets (ci_agent, security_reviewer) - should be BLOCKED BY the QA ticket

Evaluate whether the agent correctly set up these blocking relationships when creating tickets. Look at tool calls for create_ticket or Tickets___create_ticket and check the blocked_by parameter in the session context.
